name: Milnor.critPoints
textbook: Critical point of a smooth map f: M → N between smooth manifolds (Milnor §2 / Sard's theorem, p. 10): a point x of M at which the differential df_x: T_xM → T_{f(x)}N is not surjective. The set of all such points is the critical set C.
note: Tangent-map-level notion; manifold version of the same notion as Sard.critSet

name: Milnor.IsSliceSubmanifold
textbook: Embedded (regular) smooth submanifold of a smooth manifold: a subset S of M such that every point of S has a coordinate (slice) chart of M, i.e. a diffeomorphism from an open neighbourhood in M onto an open subset of ℝ^k × ℝ^l carrying S exactly onto the points of the form (z, 0). (Standard text, e.g. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, slice charts; Milnor §2 uses smooth submanifolds.)
note: Project parametrises by model spaces Z, W

name: Milnor.IsSliceSubmanifold.chartedSpace
note: Charted-space structure induced on the submanifold from the slice charts

name: Milnor.SliceChart
textbook: Slice (submanifold) chart for a subset S of a smooth manifold M: a diffeomorphism from an open set of M onto an open subset of ℝ^k × ℝ^l under which S ∩ domain corresponds exactly to the points (z, 0). (Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, ch. 5.)
note: Includes a base point x₀ in S in the domain

name: Milnor.SliceChart.invChart
note: Inverse of the induced chart with a junk value outside target

name: Milnor.SliceChart.toChart
note: Chart on S induced by a slice chart (first coordinate projection)

name: Milnor.SliceChart.x₀
note: base point field

name: Milnor.SliceChart.φ
note: the chart diffeomorphism field

name: PartialDiffeomorph.restrOpen
note: restriction of a partial diffeomorphism to an open subset of its source

name: Milnor.Sard.critSet
textbook: Critical point and critical set of a smooth map f: U → ℝ^n from an open set U ⊆ ℝ^m (Milnor §3 / Sard's theorem, p. 10): a point x ∈ U is critical if the Jacobian (differential) df_x: ℝ^m → ℝ^n is not surjective (rank < n).
note: Euclidean version of critical set; used in Sard

name: Milnor.Sphere.Sph
textbook: The unit n-sphere Sⁿ = {x ∈ ℝ^{n+1} : |x| = 1} as a subset of Euclidean space (Milnor §1/§5 etc., standard).
note: As a set only; manifold structure elsewhere

name: Milnor.Sphere.sphG
note: defining function x ↦ |x|² (-1) of the sphere, bookkeeping for regular value argument

name: Milnor.mfd
note: mfderiv typed as a linear map between model vector spaces (coercion/bookkeeping)

name: Milnor.Problems.normalBundleSet
textbook: Total space of the normal bundle of a submanifold M ⊆ ℝ^k: pairs (x, v) with x ∈ M and v ∈ ℝ^k orthogonal to the tangent space T_xM (Milnor §6 / tubular neighbourhood, standard text).
note: Lives in ℝ^k × ℝ^k; tangent space = range of derivative of inclusion

name: Milnor.Problems.normalSum
note: the map (x, v) ↦ x + v on the normal bundle used for tubular neighbourhood

name: Morse.MapTelRel
note: gluing relation used to define the quotient mapping telescope

name: Morse.MappingTelescope
textbook: Mapping telescope of a sequence of continuous maps F₀ → F₁ → F₂ → ⋯: the quotient of the disjoint union of F_n × [0,1] in which (k,1) in the n-th piece is identified with (c_n(k), 0) in the (n+1)-th piece (Milnor, Appendix, p. 149-152; standard text, e.g. Hatcher §4.G, Algebraic Topology).
note: Used to define homotopy type of a countable cell complex

name: Morse.MappingTelescope.desc
note: maps out of mapping telescope given block by block (universal property)

name: Morse.MappingTelescope.level
note: real-valued level function n+t on the telescope

name: Morse.MappingTelescope.mk
note: point inclusion (quotient map) of block n into the telescope

name: Morse.MappingTelescope.trunc
note: truncation T_n = {level ≤ n} used in proof

name: Morse.tmap
note: structure map F(m ≤ n) of the sequence, reindexing from the functor

name: Morse.CellTower
textbook: Countable CW (cell) complex presented by finite stages: K₀ obtained from a point/empty set by attaching finitely many cells, and K_{n+1} obtained from K_n by attaching finitely many cells along continuous attaching maps, K_n a subcomplex of K_{n+1} (Milnor Appendix / Theorem 17.3; Whitehead, Hatcher Appendix on CW complexes).
note: Project model of countable CW complexes as a tower; dimensions given as lists

name: Morse.CellTower.K
note: stages and inclusions bundled as a functor

name: Morse.IsCountableCellComplexType
textbook: X has the homotopy type of a CW complex with countably many cells (of given dimensions, attached in a given order) (Milnor §17 Theorem 17.3, Appendix; standard text, e.g. Hatcher ch. 4).
note: Encoded via homotopy equivalence with mapping telescope of a cell tower

name: Morse.IsRelCellAttachment
textbook: Relative CW complex obtained from a space L by attaching cells of specified dimensions one at a time: K is an iterated adjunction space L ∪_{φ₁} e^{d₁} ∪_{φ₂} e^{d₂} ∪ ⋯, each along an arbitrary continuous attaching map from the boundary sphere S^{d-1} (Milnor §3 p. 14 and Appendix; Hatcher ch. 0 / ch. 4).
note: Cell attachment along arbitrary continuous map

name: Morse.compareMap
note: comparison map from mapping telescope of the K_n to X_Σ, proof device

name: Morse.compareStrip
note: block formula for comparison map (Milnor's G, p. 152)

name: Morse.mappingTelescopeMap
note: map of mapping telescopes induced by f

name: Morse.subspaceFunctor
note: sequence of subspace inclusions as a functor ℕ ⥤ TopCat

name: Morse.IsHomotopyDirectLimit
textbook: Homotopy direct limit (Milnor Appendix p. 149): a space X is the homotopy direct limit of a sequence of subspaces X₀ ⊆ X₁ ⊆ ⋯ if the projection p: X_Σ → X from the telescope X_Σ = ⋃ X_n × [n, n+1] ⊆ X × ℝ is a homotopy equivalence.
note: Uses telescope as subset of X × ℝ

name: Morse.IsHomotopyEquiv
textbook: Homotopy equivalence (Milnor §3 p. 12): a continuous map f: X → Y for which there is g: Y → X with g∘f homotopic to id_X and f∘g homotopic to id_Y.
note: Prop-valued; Mathlib has structure

name: Morse.restrictTo
note: restriction of a map to subsets when it maps one into the other

name: Morse.stripMap
note: strip parametrisation X_n × [0,1] → X_Σ, (x,t) ↦ (x, n+t)

name: Morse.telescope
textbook: Telescope X_Σ of a sequence X₀ ⊆ X₁ ⊆ ⋯ of subspaces of X (Milnor Appendix p. 149): X_Σ = X₀ × [0,1] ∪ X₁ × [1,2] ∪ X₂ × [2,3] ∪ ⋯ topologised as a subspace of X × ℝ.
note: Subset of X × ℝ with subspace topology

name: Morse.telescopeDesc
note: maps out of X_Σ built strip by strip

name: Morse.telescopeLift
note: maps out of P × X_Σ built strip by strip with parameter space

name: Morse.telescopeMap
note: induced map f_Σ of telescopes (x,τ) ↦ (f x, τ)

name: Morse.telescopeProj
note: projection (x, τ) ↦ x from telescope to X

name: Morse.truncation
note: truncation X^n_Σ of the telescope, used in proof

name: Morse.up
note: inclusion X_n ⊆ X_{n+1}

name: Morse.IsMilnorMap
note: properties characterising Milnor's h₁, proof device

note: Milnor's homotopy u ↦ h_u on telescope, proof of Theorem A case 1

name: Morse.case1Fun
note: explicit strip formula of h_u

name: Morse.case1Map
note: h_u at a fixed time

name: Morse.case2Inv
note: Milnor's map G: Y_Σ → X_Σ, proof of Theorem A case 2

name: Morse.case2InvStrip
note: strip formula of G

name: Morse.reparam
note: reparametrisation (x, n+t) ↦ (x, n+ρ(t)) of telescope

name: Morse.scaleI
note: t ↦ min(c t, 1) scaling on unit interval

name: Morse.scaleMap
note: Milnor's R_c on the telescope, proof device

name: Morse.IsCriticalPointM
textbook: Critical point of a smooth real-valued function f on a smooth manifold M (Milnor §2, p. 4): a point p at which the induced map f_*: TM_p → T ℝ_{f(p)} is zero; equivalently, in any local coordinate system all first partial derivatives of f vanish at p.
note: Manifold version

name: Morse.IsMorseFunction
textbook: Morse function (Milnor §2, pp. 4-6): a smooth real-valued function on a smooth manifold all of whose critical points are non-degenerate.

name: Morse.IsNondegenerateCriticalPointM
textbook: Non-degenerate critical point (Milnor §2, pp. 4-5): a critical point p of a smooth function f such that the Hessian f_** on the tangent space TM_p is a non-degenerate bilinear form (in local coordinates, the matrix of second partial derivatives (∂²f/∂x^i∂x^j)(p) is non-singular).

name: Morse.IsSmoothCoord
textbook: Smooth local coordinate system on a smooth manifold (Milnor §1/§2): a diffeomorphism from an open subset of M onto an open subset of a Euclidean (normed) space, i.e. a smooth chart (y¹,…,yⁿ).
note: Allows values in an arbitrary normed space E'

name: Morse.hessianM
textbook: Hessian of a smooth function f at a critical point p of a smooth manifold (Milnor §2, pp. 4-5): the symmetric bilinear form f_** on TM_p given by f_**(v,w) = ṽ(w̃ f)(p) for any extensions ṽ, w̃ of v, w to vector fields; in local coordinates it is the matrix of second partial derivatives, and it is independent of the coordinate system at a critical point.
note: Textbook defines Hessian only at critical points

name: Morse.indexM
textbook: Index of a smooth function f at a (non-degenerate) critical point p (Milnor §2, p. 5): the index of the Hessian f_** on TM_p, i.e. the maximal dimension of a subspace of TM_p on which f_** is negative definite.

name: Morse.localRep
note: function read in preferred chart at p; bookkeeping for defining the Hessian

name: Morse.nullityM
textbook: Nullity of f at a critical point p (Milnor §2, p. 5): the nullity of the Hessian f_** on TM_p, i.e. the dimension of its null space.

name: Morse.sliceParam
note: local parametrisation of submanifold N from a slice chart

name: Morse.tangentSubspace
textbook: Tangent space T_qN of a smooth submanifold N of a vector space V (Milnor §2 / §6; standard text) at q ∈ N: the linear subspace of V of velocity vectors γ'(0) of smooth curves γ in N with γ(0) = q; equivalently the image of the differential of a local parametrisation (or of the inclusion N → V).

name: Morse.IsCriticalPoint
textbook: Critical point of a differentiable real function f on a vector space (open subset of a normed space) (Milnor §2, p. 4): a point p at which the derivative df_p = 0 (all partial derivatives vanish).
note: Vector-space version of critical point

name: Morse.IsNondegenerate
textbook: Non-degenerate bilinear form (Milnor §2, p. 5): a bilinear form H on a real vector space is non-degenerate if its null space {v : H(v,w) = 0 for all w} is trivial, i.e. nullity 0.

name: Morse.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint
textbook: Non-degenerate critical point of a function f on a vector space (Milnor §2, pp. 4-5): a critical point p where the Hessian bilinear form of f at p is non-degenerate.
note: Vector-space version

name: Morse.hessian
textbook: Hessian of a function f at a point p of a vector space (Milnor §2, pp. 4-5): the symmetric bilinear form given by the second derivative d²f_p, with matrix of second partial derivatives (∂²f/∂x^i∂x^j)(p).

name: Morse.index
textbook: Index of a symmetric bilinear form H on a real vector space (Milnor §2, p. 5): the maximal dimension of a subspace on which H is negative definite.
note: Project uses signature count of quadratic form

name: Morse.nullSpace
textbook: Null space of a symmetric bilinear form H on a vector space (Milnor §2, p. 5): the subspace of all v with H(v,w) = 0 for every w.

name: Morse.nullity
textbook: Nullity of a symmetric bilinear form (Milnor §2, p. 5): the dimension of its null space.

name: Morse.quadForm
note: quadratic form v ↦ H(v,v) from a bilinear form, bookkeeping

name: Morse.BrokenSetup
note: bundled choice of data (points, energy bound, epsilon, subdivision) for Milnor's section 16 proof

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.IsBroken
textbook: Broken geodesic with respect to a subdivision 0=t₀<…<t_k=1 of [0,1] (Milnor §16, p. 88): a piecewise smooth path whose restriction to each [t_{i-1}, t_i] is a geodesic; the set of such paths is Ω(t₀,…,t_k).
note: Relative to BrokenSetup subdivision

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.energy'
note: finite sum Σ ρ(x_i,x_{i+1})²/(t_{i+1}-t_i) used to state the energy formula

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.joinVec

name: Morse.Subdivision
textbook: Subdivision (partition) of the interval [0,1] (Milnor §16, p. 88): a finite sequence 0 = t₀ < t₁ < ⋯ < t_k = 1.
note: Parametrised by number of interior points

name: Morse.Subdivision.breaks

name: Morse.Subdivision.segOf

name: Morse.Subdivision.t
note: division points

name: Morse.closedRiemBall
textbook: Closed ball of radius r about p in a Riemannian (sub)manifold N with respect to its intrinsic distance ρ, ρ(x,y) = infimum of lengths of piecewise smooth paths in N from x to y (Milnor §10 p. 55 and §16 p. 89): {x ∈ N : ρ(p,x) ≤ r}.
note: Depends on ρ

name: Morse.vert
note: vertices of a broken path, reindexing p, y_0..y_{m-1}, q

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.chartBrokenEquiv
note: isomorphism Λ from chart coordinates to broken Jacobi fields, proof device

name: Morse.chartTangentEquiv
note: derivative of product-chart parametrisation as isomorphism, proof device

note: Milnor's Int Ω(t₀,…,t_k)^c, set of broken geodesics of energy less than c, proof device

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.brokenEquiv
note: identification of broken Jacobi fields with product of tangent spaces, proof device

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.brokenNodeMap
note: evaluation of broken Jacobi fields at break points, proof device

name: Morse.pathSpHomotopyEquiv
note: homotopy equivalence between path spaces from a path q to q' (Lemma 17.D), proof device

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.deform
note: Milnor's deformation r_u of the path space

note: homotopy equivalence Ω^a ≃ B^a built from the retraction

name: Morse.BrokenSetup.geodIndex
note: natural-number-valued index of E_** at a broken geodesic, junk 0 outside domain

name: Morse.JoinSystem
note: abstracted system of minimal joins (Lemma 17.B), proof device

name: Morse.PathC
textbook: The space Ω*(M; p, q) of all continuous paths [0,1] → M from p to q, with the compact-open (uniform) topology (Milnor §17, p. 93).
note: Type form of pathCSet

name: Morse.PathSp.toC
note: underlying continuous map of a piecewise smooth path, coercion

name: Morse.PathSp.toPathC
note: inclusion Ω → Ω* (Milnor p. 93), coercion between path spaces

name: Morse.pathCSet
textbook: The space Ω*(M; p, q) of all continuous paths [0,1] → M from p to q, topologised as a subspace of C([0,1], M) with the compact-open topology, which for a metric space agrees with the uniform topology (Milnor §17, p. 93).
note: Set form; M here is submanifold N of V

name: Morse.pathIncl
note: inclusion i: Ω → Ω* as a continuous map (Theorem 17.1 statement)

name: Morse.geodesicIndex
textbook: Index of a geodesic γ from p to q (Milnor §13 and Theorem 15.1): the index of the Hessian E_** of the energy function E on the path space Ω(M; p, q) at γ, i.e. the maximal dimension of a subspace of the tangent space TΩ_γ on which E_** is negative definite.
note: Natural-number-valued; finite by index theorem

name: Morse.PathSp
textbook: Path space Ω(M; p, q) (Milnor §13 p. 67 and §16 p. 88): the space of piecewise smooth paths [0,1] → M from p to q, with the metric d(ω, ω') = max_t ρ(ω(t), ω'(t)) + (∫₀¹ (|dω/dt| − |dω'/dt|)² dt)^{1/2}, where ρ is the Riemannian distance on M.
note: Carries Milnor's metric; paths are functions ℝ → V in project

name: Morse.PathSp.l2Dist
note: L² part of Milnor's metric on Ω, component of metric

name: Morse.PathSp.speed

note: Milnor's geodesic γ_k on the sphere (p. 95)

name: Morse.sphLen
note: length L(γ_k) of Milnor's k-th geodesic on the sphere

name: Morse.expDiffeomorph
note: exp_p is a diffeomorphism under completeness and non-positive curvature (conclusion of Theorem 19.2 proof)

name: Morse.NonposCurvature
textbook: Non-positive curvature of a Riemannian manifold (Milnor §19, p. 100, Lemma 19.1 / Theorem 19.2): every sectional curvature K(σ) of every tangent 2-plane σ is ≤ 0; in Milnor's sign convention ⟨R(A,B)A,B⟩ ≤ 0 for all tangent vectors A, B at every point.
note: Hypothesis of Cartan-Hadamard; project proves equivalence with sectional curvature

name: Morse.dExpAt
note: derivative of exp_q at v as linear map into ambient V

name: Morse.expDomAt
textbook: Domain of the exponential map exp_q at a point q of a Riemannian manifold (Milnor §10, p. 55; §18): the set of tangent vectors v ∈ T_qN for which the geodesic with initial velocity v is defined on [0,1]; open, and all of T_qN when N is complete.
note: Domain part of exp definition

name: Morse.expJacobi
note: Jacobi field of the variation exp_q(t(v+uX)), proof device for Theorem 18.1

name: Morse.RicciLowerBound
textbook: Ricci curvature lower bound hypothesis of Myers' theorem (Milnor §19, Theorem 19.4, p. 104): Ricci curvature K(U,U) ≥ (n−1)/r² for every unit tangent vector U at every point of an n-dimensional Riemannian manifold N.
note: Real parameter r

name: Morse.ricci
textbook: Ricci curvature of a Riemannian manifold (Milnor §19, p. 104): the symmetric bilinear form K(U₁,U₂) on T_qN equal to the trace of the linear map W ↦ R(U₁,W)U₂, R the curvature tensor in Milnor's sign convention (§9).
note: Submanifold-of-V setting; K(U,U) is sum of sectional curvatures

name: Morse.conjLocus
textbook: Conjugate locus of a point p of a Riemannian manifold N (Milnor §15 p. 77 and §19 p. 99): the set of points q conjugate to p along some geodesic from p to q, where q = γ(1) is conjugate to p = γ(0) along γ if there is a non-trivial Jacobi field along γ vanishing at both ends.
note: Depends on conjugate-point notion

name: Morse.ricciMap
note: linear map W ↦ R(Pu,PW)Pu whose trace is the Ricci curvature, helper

name: Morse.IsAdInvariant
textbook: Ad-invariant (bi-invariant) bilinear form on a Lie algebra 𝔤 (Milnor §21.3(a), p. 123): ⟨[X,Y],Z⟩ = ⟨X,[Y,Z]⟩ for all X, Y, Z ∈ 𝔤; corresponds to a bi-invariant metric on the Lie group.

name: Morse.IsLeviCivita
textbook: Levi-Civita (Riemannian) connection restricted to left-invariant vector fields on a Lie group (Milnor §8, 8.4-8.5 and §21): a connection D which is symmetric (D_X Y − D_Y X = [X,Y]) and compatible with the metric (X⟨Y,Z⟩ = ⟨D_X Y,Z⟩ + ⟨Y,D_X Z⟩).
note: Pointwise on Lie algebra of left-invariant fields

name: Morse.centerCompl
note: Corollary 21.6: orthogonal complement of the centre is an ideal, proof device

name: Morse.curv
textbook: Riemann curvature tensor R(X,Y)Z of a connection (Milnor §9, p. 51), in Milnor's sign convention (opposite to R = ∇_X∇_Y − ∇_Y∇_X − ∇_{[X,Y]}), so that the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by orthonormal X, Y is ⟨R(X,Y)X,Y⟩; here evaluated on left-invariant fields of a Lie group.
note: Lie-algebra-level formula

name: Morse.halfLie
note: connection X ⊢ Y = ½[X,Y] of a bi-invariant metric (21.3(d))

name: Morse.jacobiOp
note: Jacobi operator K_V(W) = R(V,W)V = −¼(Ad V)²W for Lie groups, formula

name: Morse.jacK

name: Morse.IsMatrixGroup
textbook: Compact Lie group G with its Lie algebra 𝔤 (Milnor §21, p. 121-125 and Part IV): here realised as a closed subgroup G of the unitary group U(n) (a compact matrix group) and its Lie algebra 𝔤 = {X skew-Hermitian: exp(tX) ∈ G for all t}, the tangent space of G at the identity, with dim G = dim 𝔤.
note: Project encodes via closure under product/inverse, Ad-invariance, exp 𝔤 ⊆ G, dims equal

name: Morse.hermitian
note: real subspace of Hermitian matrices

name: Morse.specialSkewHermitian
textbook: The Lie algebra 𝔰𝔲(n) (Milnor p. 126): the real Lie algebra of skew-Hermitian complex n×n matrices of trace 0, the Lie algebra of the special unitary group SU(n).

name: Morse.MatrixInner.innerProductSpace
textbook: Frobenius (Hilbert-Schmidt) inner product on the space of n×n matrices (Milnor §21, p. 125): ⟨A,B⟩ = Re tr(AB*), inducing the bi-invariant Riemannian metric on U(n), SU(n), Sp(n).
note: Real inner product on matrices over ℝ, ℂ or ℍ-like fields

note: U(1) ≅ S^1 homeomorphism via determinant

name: Morse.milnorM
textbook: The numbers m_k (Milnor §24, p. 143): m_k is the least dimension of a real vector space carrying k pairwise anticommuting complex structures (equivalently the dimension of an irreducible module over the Clifford algebra), with values 1,2,4,4,8,8,8,8,16 for k=0,…,8 and m_{k+8} = 16 m_k.
note: Unsure: project defines by table; textbook defn recalled from memory

name: Morse.milnorM.match_1
note: compiler-generated match auxiliary

name: Morse.IsAnticommFamily
textbook: Family of anticommuting complex structures (Milnor §24, p. 136): matrices J₁,…,J_k on ℝⁿ, each a complex structure (orthogonal with J² = −I), with J_iJ_j = −J_jJ_i for i ≠ j.
note: Standing assumption on indexed family

name: Morse.IsComplexStructure
textbook: Complex structure on ℝⁿ (Milnor §24, p. 133): an orthogonal linear transformation J of ℝⁿ with J² = −I.
note: Orthogonal complex structure (Milnor's version)

name: Morse.Omega
textbook: The space Ω_k(n) (Milnor §24, p. 136): with J₁,…,J_{k-1} fixed anticommuting complex structures on ℝⁿ, Ω_0(n) = O(n) and for k ≥ 1, Ω_k(n) is the space of all complex structures J on ℝⁿ that anticommute with J₁,…,J_{k-1}.
note: Topologised as a subspace of matrices

name: Morse.Omega.match_1
note: compiler-generated match auxiliary

name: Morse.omegaPhi
note: Milnor's φ_r: Ω_{k+1}(n) → Ω(Ω_k(n); J_k, -J_k), semicircle map (p. 138)

name: Morse.stratumIn
note: stratum viewed inside Ω_k(n), subtype helper

name: Morse.omegaStratum
note: stratum (component-wise dimension) of Ω_k(n) through p, bookkeeping for non-constant dimension

name: Morse.tanAlg
note: Milnor's 𝒯_J (Lemma 24.4), tangent-space-like subspace

name: Morse.basePt
note: Milnor's base point J_k of Ω_k(n)

name: Morse.minVelO
note: initial directions of minimal geodesics in Ω_k(n)

name: Morse.minVelOHomeomorph
note: homeomorphism A ↦ J_kA of Lemma 24.4 (iii)

name: Morse.minVelToOmegaPaths
note: map A ↦ geodesic t ↦ p exp(πtA)

name: Morse.omegaGeo
note: geodesic t ↦ p exp(πtA)

name: Morse.omegaMinPathsHomotopyEquiv
note: homotopy equivalence of Lemma 24.4 (iii) between initial directions and minimal geodesics

name: Morse.omegaPath
note: geodesic as a point of the path space

name: Morse.omegaPathsToMinVel
note: midpoint map from minimal geodesics to initial directions

name: Morse.IsCentralI
note: Milnor's i = J₁⋯J_{k-1}, axiomatised

name: Morse.iWordM
note: word J_1⋯J_{k-1}, helper

name: Morse.omegaComp
note: Milnor's Ω^{(c)} subspace of the path space of Ω_k(n) by winding angle

name: Morse.omegaF
note: Milnor's f(X) = det_ℂ(J^{-1}X), winding function

name: Morse.IsAngleLift
textbook: Continuous determination of the angle (argument) of a path t ↦ F(ω(t)) in ℂ∖{0} on [0,1], starting at 0: a continuous real-valued function θ with F(ω(t)) = |F(ω(t))| e^{i(arg F(ω(0)) + θ(t))} (Milnor §24, winding argument; lift through covering ℝ → S¹).
note: Predicate form

name: Morse.cdet
textbook: Complex determinant det_ℂ of a real linear map commuting with a complex structure J on ℝ^{2m}: the determinant of the induced complex-linear map on (ℝ^{2m}, J) ≅ ℂ^m (Milnor §24, p. 140).
note: Encoded via complexification and eigenprojections

name: Morse.cplx
note: complexification of a real matrix

name: Morse.projM
note: eigenprojection P₋ of complex structure

name: Morse.projP
note: eigenprojection P₊ of complex structure

name: Morse.windSet
note: Milnor's Ω^{(c)}: paths with prescribed angle at end

name: Morse.AttachCell
textbook: Adjunction space X ∪_φ e^n obtained by attaching an n-cell to X along a continuous map φ: ∂Dⁿ = S^{n-1} → X (Milnor §3, p. 13; Hatcher ch. 0): the quotient of the disjoint union X ⊔ Dⁿ by the identification x ~ φ(x) for x ∈ ∂Dⁿ.
note: Pushout in TopCat

name: Morse.cellInl
note: inclusion X → X ∪_φ e^n

name: Morse.clampI
note: clamping real number to [0,1]

name: Morse.IsCellAttachment
textbook: Space obtained from the empty space by attaching cells of listed dimensions one after another, each along an arbitrary continuous attaching map from the boundary sphere into the space built so far (iterated adjunction space; Milnor §3, p. 14 and Theorem 3.5).
note: Iterated adjunction spaces, dimensions from a list

name: Morse.IsFiniteCellComplexType
textbook: X has the homotopy type of a finite cell (CW) complex with cells of given dimensions (Milnor §3, Theorem 3.5, p. 20): X is homotopy equivalent to a space built from the empty set by successively attaching cells of those dimensions along continuous attaching maps.
note: Cells in listed order

name: Morse.IsSplitMorseChart
textbook: Morse coordinates (Milnor §2, Lemma 2.2, p. 6): near a non-degenerate critical point p of a smooth function f of index λ, a local coordinate system (u¹,…,uⁿ) centred at p (u^i(p) = 0) on a neighbourhood U with f = f(p) − (u¹)² − ⋯ − (u^λ)² + (u^{λ+1})² + ⋯ + (uⁿ)² throughout U.
note: Coordinates split into (x,y) with ξ=‖x‖², η=‖y‖²

name: Morse.cellE
note: Milnor's cell e^λ = {ξ ≤ ε, η = 0}, proof of Theorem 3.2

name: Morse.milnorBump
note: correction term μ(ξ+2η) transported by chart

name: Morse.milnorF
note: Milnor's modified function F = f − μ(ξ+2η) (p. 16)

name: Morse.CellModel.cellModel
note: Milnor's cell e^λ in model coordinates

name: Morse.CellModel.eta
note: η = ‖y‖² in model coordinates

name: Morse.CellModel.morseQuad
note: model Morse function f = c − ξ + η

name: Morse.CellModel.retractModel
note: Milnor's deformation r_t in model coordinates (pp. 18-19)

name: Morse.CellModel.retractScale
note: shrinking factor σ_t used in r_t

name: Morse.CellModel.xi
note: ξ = ‖x‖² in model coordinates

name: Morse.IsMilnorMu
note: conditions on Milnor's bump function μ (p. 16)

name: Morse.milnorMu
note: explicit bump μ satisfying Milnor's conditions

name: Morse.muBump
note: plateau function β for μ

name: Morse.IsMorsePatch
textbook: Morse coordinates for a function on a topological space (topological version of Morse's lemma chart, Milnor Lemma 2.2 as used on p. 15): a homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of p onto an open subset of X × Y carrying p to 0 with f = f(p) − ‖x‖² + ‖y‖².
note: Topological (non-smooth) version used in cell attachment

name: Morse.patchBump
note: correction term transported by patch

name: Morse.patchF
note: Milnor's F = f − μ(ξ+2η) on a patch

name: Morse.IsSlabFlow
note: abstract flow situation of proof of Theorem 3.1

name: Morse.IsStrongDeformationRetract
textbook: Strong deformation retract (Milnor §3, p. 13): a subspace A of X is a deformation retract of X if there is a homotopy r_t: X → X, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, with r_0 = id, r_1(X) ⊆ A and r_t(a) = a for all a ∈ A and all t (r_1 is then a retraction of X onto A).
note: Milnor's 'deformation retract' is this strong version

name: Morse.sublevel
textbook: Sublevel set M^c = f^{-1}(−∞, c] = {p ∈ M : f(p) ≤ c} of a real-valued function f on M (Milnor §3, p. 12).

name: Morse.chartDomain
note: union of slice chart domains, helper open set

name: Morse.critCount
textbook: Morse number C_λ (Milnor §5, p. 29): the number of critical points of index λ of a Morse function f on M (when finite).

name: Morse.FiltrationHomology
note: abstract homology-sequence-of-triple data for filtrations

name: Morse.LongExactSeq
note: abstract long exact sequence shape of homology of a triple, proof device for Morse inequalities

name: Morse.LongExactSeq.f
note: first map of the long exact sequence

name: Morse.altSum
note: truncated alternating sum used to state Morse inequalities

name: Morse.morseNumber
note: Morse numbers of a chain in terms of relative homology dimensions

name: Morse.Torus.height
note: Milnor's height function on the torus (Diagram 1)

name: Morse.torus
textbook: Torus of revolution in ℝ³ (Milnor §1, p. 1, Diagram 1): the surface obtained by rotating a circle of radius r about an axis in its plane at distance R > r from its centre, {x : (√(x₁²+x₂²) − R)² + x₃² = r²}.
note: Example

name: Morse.IsFocalPoint
textbook: Focal point of (M, q) (Milnor §6, p. 32): for a smooth submanifold M ⊂ ℝⁿ, a point e is a focal point of (M, q), q ∈ M, if e = q + v with v a vector normal to M at q such that the endpoint map E: N → ℝⁿ, E(q,v) = q + v, on the normal bundle N of M has Jacobian at (q,v) with positive nullity (of any multiplicity).
note: M a slice submanifold of ℝⁿ with k+w=n

name: Morse.IsFocalPointMult
textbook: Focal point of (M, q) with multiplicity μ (Milnor §6, p. 32): e = q + v, (q,v) ∈ normal bundle N of M ⊂ ℝⁿ, and the Jacobian of the endpoint map E(q,v) = q + v at (q,v) has nullity μ > 0 (nullity = dimension of the kernel of the differential).

name: Morse.endpointNullity
note: nullity of the Jacobian of the endpoint map at a normal-bundle point; helper for the focal point definition

name: Morse.focalSet
textbook: Set of focal points of a submanifold M ⊂ ℝⁿ (Milnor §6, p. 32): the points that are focal points of (M, q) for some q ∈ M.

name: Morse.ballDiffeo
note: diffeomorphism ℝⁿ → open unit ball y ↦ y/√(1+|y|²), used in uniform-bound argument

name: Morse.toBall
note: restriction of ball diffeomorphism to M

name: Morse.IsComplexSubmanifold
textbook: Complex submanifold of a complex vector space ℂᵐ = ℝ^{2m} (Milnor §7, p. 39 ff): a smooth real submanifold N whose tangent spaces are complex subspaces, i.e. J(T_xN) ⊆ T_xN where J is multiplication by i.
note: Complex structure J as real linear map

name: Morse.IsOrthComplexStructure
textbook: Complex structure on a Euclidean space as multiplication by i (Milnor §7 / §24 p. 133): an orthogonal linear map J with J² = −1.
note: Linear-map version of IsComplexStructure

name: Morse.HypothesisN
textbook: Hypothesis (N) of Milnor §7 (p. 42): the subspace A of X has a neighbourhood U in X that can be deformed into A within X by a homotopy keeping A pointwise fixed (A is a neighbourhood deformation retract-like subspace).
note: Not a named standard notion

name: Morse.CP.Cn
note: ℂⁿ as real inner product space, typeclass bookkeeping

name: Morse.CP.aff
note: affine chart of projective space minus hyperplane

name: Morse.CP.affineHomeomorph
note: homeomorphism of affine chart

name: Morse.CP.affinePart
note: affine part of a subset of projective space

name: Morse.CP.cpxJ
note: multiplication by i on ℝ^{2n} via isometry

name: Morse.CP.hyperplaneSection
note: hyperplane section V ∩ P of a subset of projective space

name: Morse.CP.lift
note: vector (1,u) in ℂ^{n+1}

name: Morse.CP.mulI
note: multiplication by i as real linear map

name: Morse.CP.nc
note: 1+|u|² as complex number

name: Morse.CP.proj
note: inverse of affine chart

name: Morse.CP.theta
note: isometry ℂⁿ ≅ ℝ^{2n}

name: Morse.IsCompatible
textbook: Compatibility of a connection with a Riemannian metric (Milnor §8, p. 47-48, Cor. 8.4): X⟨Y,Y'⟩ = ⟨D_X Y, Y'⟩ + ⟨Y, D_X Y'⟩ for vector fields X, Y, Y'; equivalently parallel translation preserves inner products.
note: Mathlib CovariantDerivative on tangent bundle

name: Morse.dN
note: derivative of a map on N applied to ambient tangent vectors; coordinate bookkeeping

name: Morse.sliceAt
note: chosen slice chart at a point

name: Morse.tanCoord
note: chart coordinates of an ambient vector, bookkeeping

name: Morse.tanProj
textbook: Orthogonal projection P_q of the ambient Euclidean space V onto the tangent space T_qN of a submanifold N ⊆ V at q (Milnor §8, p. 43).

name: Morse.covAt
textbook: Covariant derivative X_p ⊢ Y of a vector field Y on a submanifold N ⊆ ℝⁿ in the direction of a tangent vector X_p (Milnor §8, p. 43): the tangential component (orthogonal projection onto TN_p) of the ordinary directional derivative of Y.
note: Induced Riemannian connection

name: Morse.curvOp
note: curvature expressed via derivative of tangent projection, formula

name: Morse.curvTensor
textbook: Riemann curvature tensor R of a submanifold N ⊆ ℝⁿ with induced metric (Milnor §9, p. 51, Lemma 9.1): the trilinear map R(X,Y)Z on T_qN, in Milnor's sign convention (so that the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by orthonormal X, Y is ⟨R(X,Y)X,Y⟩, and the unit sphere has curvature +1); expressible by the second fundamental form via the Gauss equation.
note: Project formula R(x,y)z = II(y,II(x,z)) - II(x,II(y,z))

name: Morse.secondFundForm
textbook: Second fundamental form II of a submanifold N ⊆ ℝⁿ at q (standard text; Milnor §8-9): the normal component of the derivative of a tangent vector field, II(v,w) = (1−P_q)(dW_q(v)) for a tangent field W with W(q)=w, symmetric and normal-valued.
note: Project defines via derivative of the tangent projection

name: Morse.IsShortJoin
note: conclusion of Corollary 10.8 packaged as a predicate (unique short geodesic depending smoothly on endpoints)

name: Morse.pathLengths
note: set of lengths of piecewise smooth paths, helper for the distance

name: Morse.riemDist
textbook: Riemannian distance ρ(p, q) on a connected Riemannian manifold or submanifold N (Milnor §10, p. 62): the greatest lower bound of the lengths of piecewise smooth paths in N from p to q.
note: Extended-real valued, ∞ if none

name: Morse.IsGeodesicFrom
note: geodesic through q with initial velocity v defined on an open interval around [0,1], helper for exp

name: Morse.exp
textbook: Exponential map exp_q: for a Riemannian manifold or submanifold N and q ∈ N (Milnor §10, p. 57): exp_q(v) = γ(1), where γ is the geodesic with γ(0) = q and γ'(0) = v, defined for those v ∈ T_qN for which this geodesic exists on [0,1].
note: Total function in project, junk value q outside domain

name: Morse.expDom
textbook: Domain of the exponential map (Milnor §10, p. 57): the set of pairs (q, v) with v ∈ T_qN such that the geodesic with γ(0) = q, γ'(0) = v is defined on an open interval containing [0, 1].

name: Morse.IsGeodesicOn
textbook: Geodesic of a Riemannian manifold or submanifold N (Milnor §8-§10, p. 55): a smooth curve γ: I → N whose velocity vector field has zero covariant derivative, D/dt(dγ/dt) = 0; for N ⊆ ℝⁿ with the induced metric, equivalently the acceleration γ'' is everywhere orthogonal to N.
note: Defined on an open set of times

name: Morse.IsGeodesicallyComplete
textbook: Geodesic completeness (Milnor §10, pp. 58, 62): a Riemannian manifold N is geodesically complete if exp_q(v) is defined for every q ∈ N and every v ∈ T_qN; equivalently every geodesic extends to all of ℝ.

name: Morse.IsMinimalGeodesic
textbook: Minimal geodesic (Milnor §10, p. 61): a geodesic segment γ: [a,b] → N whose length is less than or equal to that of every piecewise smooth path in N with the same endpoints.

name: Morse.IsRiemBounded
textbook: Bounded subset of a Riemannian manifold N (Milnor §10, p. 64): a subset of finite diameter with respect to the Riemannian distance ρ.

name: Morse.IsRiemComplete
textbook: Completeness of the metric space (N, ρ) (Milnor §10, p. 64, Hopf-Rinow): every Cauchy sequence for the Riemannian distance ρ converges in N.

name: Morse.IsNormalRadius
textbook: Normal neighbourhood (Milnor §10, Lemma 10.3, p. 57-58): an ε-ball in the tangent space T_qN on which exp_q is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighbourhood of q in N.
note: Project term 'normal radius'

name: Morse.NormalCoord
textbook: Normal coordinates of radius ε at q (Milnor §10, p. 57-58): exp_q restricts to a diffeomorphism from the ball of radius ε in T_qN onto an open neighbourhood of q in N.
note: Bundles smooth extensions F, G

name: Morse.expToN
note: exp_q as a map T_qN → N with junk value q outside domain

name: Morse.IsAdmissible
note: auxiliary regularity class of paths (continuous, a.e. differentiable, integrable speed) used to state lemmas; not in textbook

name: Morse.IsPiecewiseSmooth
textbook: Piecewise smooth path (Milnor §10, p. 59, and §13 p. 67): a continuous map c: [a,b] → N for which there is a subdivision a = t₀ < t₁ < ⋯ < t_k = b such that c restricted to each closed subinterval [t_{i-1}, t_i] is smooth (C^∞, with one-sided derivatives at endpoints).

name: Morse.pathLength
textbook: Length of a piecewise smooth path c: [a,b] → N (Milnor §10, p. 59): L(c) = ∫ₐᵇ |dc/dt| dt.
note: Norm from ambient/induced metric

name: Morse.IsCriticalPath
textbook: Critical path of the energy function E on Ω (Milnor §12, p. 69): a path ω ∈ Ω(M; p, q) is a critical point of E if for every variation α of ω with fixed end points the derivative d/du E(α(u)) at u = 0 exists and equals zero.

name: Morse.IsUnbrokenGeodesic
textbook: Unbroken geodesic in Ω (Milnor §12, Theorem 12.3, p. 73): a path ω ∈ Ω(M;p,q) which is a (smooth) geodesic on all of [0,1], i.e. smooth with D/dt(dω/dt) = 0 on [0,1].
note: Critical points of E are exactly these

name: Morse.IsVariation
textbook: Variation of a piecewise smooth path ω with fixed end points (Milnor §11, p. 68): a function α: (−ε,ε) × [0,1] → M (or, §13, a two-parameter version on a neighbourhood of 0 ∈ ℝ²) such that α(0,·) = ω, there is a subdivision of [0,1] such that α is smooth on each strip, and α(u,0) = ω(0), α(u,1) = ω(1) for all u.
note: Open parameter set in a normed space

name: Morse.energy
textbook: Energy of a piecewise smooth path ω: [a,b] → M (Milnor §12, p. 70): E_a^b(ω) = ∫ₐᵇ |dω/dt|² dt; E(ω) means E_0^1(ω).

name: Morse.jump
textbook: Jump of the derivative (velocity) at a point t of a piecewise smooth path (Milnor §12, p. 71): Δ_t(dω/dt) = dω/dt(t⁺) − dω/dt(t⁻), the difference of the one-sided derivatives.

name: Morse.pathSpace
textbook: Path space Ω(M; p, q) (Milnor §12-13, p. 67): the set of piecewise smooth paths ω: [0,1] → M with ω(0) = p and ω(1) = q.
note: Set version, represented by functions ℝ → V

name: Morse.pathTangent
textbook: Tangent space TΩ_ω of the path space at ω (Milnor §12, p. 67-68): the vector space of piecewise smooth vector fields W along ω, tangent to M, vanishing at t = 0 and t = 1.
note: Defined as a vector space of fields

name: Morse.prj
note: total version of tangent projection (zero off N), convenient in integrands

name: Morse.varField
textbook: Variation vector field of a variation α of ω (Milnor §11-12, p. 68): W_t = ∂α/∂u(0, t).
note: 1-parameter case

name: Morse.accel
textbook: Acceleration of a piecewise smooth path ω (Milnor §12, p. 71): A_t = D/dt(dω/dt), the covariant derivative of the velocity field, defined away from break points.

name: Morse.covD
textbook: Covariant derivative D X/dt of a vector field X along a path ω in a Riemannian manifold or submanifold (Milnor §8, p. 46): in a submanifold of ℝⁿ, the tangential component of the ordinary derivative dX/dt.

name: Morse.firstVariation
note: right-hand side of first variation formula (Theorem 12.2), formula used to state the theorem

name: Morse.IsMinimalPath
textbook: Path of least length in Ω(M; p, q) (Milnor §10, p. 61): a path in Ω(M;p,q) whose length is at most that of every other path in Ω(M;p,q).

name: Morse.energyHessian
textbook: Hessian E_** of the energy function E at a geodesic γ ∈ Ω(M; p, q) (Milnor §13, p. 74): the symmetric bilinear form E_**: TΩ_γ × TΩ_γ → ℝ given by E_**(W₁,W₂) = ∂²E(α(u₁,u₂))/∂u₁∂u₂ at (0,0) for any 2-parameter variation α of γ with variation fields W₁, W₂.
note: Project defines via integral form (Thm 13.1/Prop 13.A) and proves equivalence

name: Morse.hessForm
note: Hessian in integral form, half of E_**, formula used to state Prop 13.A

name: Morse.IsJacobiField
textbook: Jacobi field along a geodesic γ (Milnor §14, p. 77): a smooth vector field J along γ satisfying the Jacobi equation D²J/dt² + R(V, J)V = 0, where V = dγ/dt and R is the curvature tensor.

name: Morse.jacobiExpr
note: Jacobi operator expression D²J/dt² + R(V,J)V, helper

name: Morse.curvR
note: total version of curvature tensor (zero off N) used in Jacobi and second variation formulas

name: Morse.secondVariation
note: right-hand side of the second variation formula (Theorem 13.1), formula

name: Morse.IsBrokenJacobi
textbook: Broken Jacobi field along γ with respect to a subdivision (Milnor §15, p. 83): a continuous piecewise smooth vector field along γ that on each segment [t_{i-1}, t_i] is a Jacobi field.

name: Morse.brokenSpace
note: space TΩ_γ(t₀,…,t_k) of broken Jacobi fields along γ|[0,τ], proof device

name: Morse.fieldsUpTo
note: fields along γ|[0,τ] vanishing at ends, extended by zero

name: Morse.IsNegDefOn
textbook: Bilinear form negative definite on a subspace S: B(v,v) < 0 for every nonzero v ∈ S.

name: Morse.formIndex
textbook: Index of a symmetric bilinear form H on a (possibly infinite-dimensional) real vector space (Milnor §2 p. 5, §15 p. 83): the maximal dimension (supremum of dimensions) of a subspace on which H is negative definite.
note: Extended-natural valued

name: Morse.indexUpTo
note: Milnor's λ(τ): index of the Hessian along γ|[0,τ], proof device in §15

name: Morse.IsConjugate
textbook: Conjugate points along a geodesic (Milnor §14, p. 77): γ(a) and γ(b), a ≠ b, are conjugate along γ if there is a Jacobi field along γ, not identically zero, vanishing at t = a and t = b.
note: Stated at parameter level

name: Morse.conjMultiplicity
textbook: Multiplicity of conjugate points (Milnor §14, p. 77): the dimension of the vector space of Jacobi fields along γ vanishing at t = a and t = b.

name: Morse.conjSpace
note: space of Jacobi fields vanishing at a and b

name: Morse.hessNullSpace
textbook: Null space of the Hessian E_** at a geodesic γ (Milnor §14, p. 77): the set of W₁ ∈ TΩ_γ with E_**(W₁, W₂) = 0 for all W₂ ∈ TΩ_γ.
note: Realised as fields on [0,1]

name: Morse.hessNullity
textbook: Nullity of the Hessian E_** at a geodesic γ (Milnor §14, p. 77): the dimension of the null space of E_**.

name: Morse.jacobiSpace
note: space of Jacobi fields along γ normalised to be constant off [0,1]

name: Morse.restrictIcc
note: restriction to [0,1] extended by constants

name: Morse.IsSmoothCurveIn
textbook: Smooth curve γ: [0,1] → N in a submanifold, C^∞ on the closed interval with values in N.

name: Morse.covAlong
note: covariant derivative along a path computed within [0,1], duplicate of covD with one-sided endpoints

name: Morse.flow
textbook: Flow of a vector field X on a vector space/manifold (Milnor §3, proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 12-13): the family φ_t of diffeomorphisms with φ_0 = id and d/dt φ_t(x) = X(φ_t(x)), the integral curves of X.
note: Chosen integral curve, junk value otherwise

name: Morse.Homology.bettiNumber
textbook: Betti number b_i(X) = dim_𝕜 H_i(X; 𝕜) of a space X over a field 𝕜 (Milnor §5, p. 28: rank R_i(X) of the i-th homology vector space).
note: Finrank, 0 if infinite-dimensional

name: Morse.Homology.spaceHomology
textbook: Singular homology H_i(X; 𝕜) of a topological space X with coefficients in a field 𝕜 (Milnor §5, p. 27; Hatcher ch. 2).

name: Morse.Homology.cokernelSequence
note: functor Arrow ⥤ ShortComplex, category-theory plumbing

name: Morse.Homology.relChains
textbook: Relative singular chain complex C(X, A; R) = C(X; R)/C(A; R) of a pair (X, A) of spaces (Hatcher ch. 2).
note: Functor on pairs

name: Morse.Homology.relHomology
textbook: Relative singular homology H_n(X, A; R) of a pair of spaces (X, A) (Milnor §3/§5, pp. 27-28; Hatcher ch. 2): homology of the quotient chain complex C(X; R)/C(A; R).
note: Functor on pairs

name: Morse.Homology.relShortComplex
note: short exact sequence C(A) → C(X) → C(X,A), plumbing

name: Morse.Homology.singularChains
textbook: Singular chain complex C_*(X; R) of a topological space with coefficients in R (Hatcher ch. 2).
note: Functor to chain complexes

name: Morse.Homology.subsetInclusion
note: inclusion of subsets as morphism of TopCat

name: Morse.Homology.subsetPair
note: pair (B, A) from a subset inclusion, bookkeeping

name: Morse.Homology.TopTriple
textbook: Triple of spaces Z ⊆ Y ⊆ X (Milnor §5, p. 30; Hatcher ch. 2): inclusions Z → Y → X.
note: Bundles i, j and composite k

name: Morse.Homology.TopTriple.X
note: big space X

name: Morse.Homology.TopTriple.Y
note: middle space Y

name: Morse.Homology.TopTriple.Z
note: small space Z

name: Morse.Homology.TopTriple.i
